newsitem.title: UK: UK utilities must protect customers, Labour says.
newsitem.headline: UK utilities must protect customers, Labour says.

text.p: A Labour government would give regulators of Britain's privatised utilities a primary duty to protect customers' interests, shadow trade and industry minister Margaret Beckett said on Monday.

In a speech at the Labour party conference, she said she planned stricter controls, a fresh look at regulators' methods and a strategy to prevent customers from being "ripped off" while ensuring proper investment for the future.

"That's why I can announce today that a Labour government will change the law to ensure that the regulators of the utility industries have a primary duty to protect customers' interests -- the interests of members of the public -- along with their duties to promote competition and ensure financial viability," Beckett added.
Labour plans a tax on the windfall profits of privatised utilities and will use the proceeds to try to reduce unemployment.
Beckett said the Conservative government had allowed the utilities to "exploit their potential to make money for the few at the expense of the many."

"That's why Labour would require that these great utility companies operate with full regard for the public and national interest -- to benefit their customers, not just their shareholders," she added.
